clue.text: Perhaps Cher's in bed, scratching bottom

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A gossip item about the pop star Cher lying in bed and scratching her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom is the last letter, so DIVAN loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Cher is a celebrated singer with star temperament, an example of a prima donna; 'Perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Initially fall in love with mass entertainment

explanation.walkthrough: 'mass entertainment' reads as one phrase, but 'mass' is just M after the three initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a form of entertainment shown in cinemas and on screens.

clue.text: Flipping focus to watch sailor boxing CGI-produced lion, say

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly switches attention to a computer-animated lion, perhaps in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CGI-produced' reads as describing the lion, but CGI is simply letters to be enclosed; the whole string is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is one example of the large wild felines collectively called by this name, alongside tigers and leopards.

clue.text: Characters in highbrow hit established as brightest

indicators.note: the letters sit consecutively within the words that follow

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'highbrow' through 'hit' into 'established'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure white is the most luminous colour, so the most white thing is the most dazzling.

clue.text: One has wings — told to taste without seasoning?

explanation.walkthrough: TRY PLAIN said aloud is the aircraft name; the definition plays on the plane having three sets of wings.
explanation.definitionFit: This early aircraft has three stacked pairs of wings, so it is one thing that has wings.

clue.text: Kettle blew up — ultimately going off fine dining

explanation.walkthrough: Kettle is a police tactic here, not a pan; 'blew up' minus each word's last letter leaves BLE and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase denotes cookery of the highest standard, so it stands for haute cuisine.

clue.text: Trouble from school next to motorway — that is loud

clue.text: Car limited by course that's lower

clue.text: Author's latest books inspired by this, but in Latin accent

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is strictly an adjective describing an accent that sounds its Rs; the setter treats it as naming such an accent.

clue.text: Tavern's opening has beer enthusiasts returning — it's over the road?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
returning sends the group's name back the way it came

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is the British group of traditional beer lovers

explanation.surface: Real-ale fans come back to a pub as it opens, and the pub is across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA is a British consumer group campaigning for traditional ale; reversed it is ARMAC.

clue.text: Retrospectively judge a republican government

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: A historian judges a republican regime in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule over India.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is the Hindi word for rule, used for British governance of India.

clue.text: Tango to mimic Diet Coke, regularly finding means of copying pop

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: taking every other letter at a regular interval

clue.text: Bring back old American guitar

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.definitionFit: Axe is musicians' slang for a guitar, especially an electric one.

clue.text: Get used to a diet short of stuffing and without gravy

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust to a situation is to adapt and become accustomed to it.

clue.text: Some smear campaigns provide spin

indicators.note: some of the letters are taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Political smear campaigns are said to provide media spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin looks like political spin, but it is a bowled ball curving through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning ball curves through the air, so to spin is loosely to arc.

clue.text: Stop visiting suspect with diamonds hidden all over the place

explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquitous means present everywhere, found in every location.

clue.text: Perhaps limpet mine finally smothered by military unit before capture

indicators.note: takes the last letter of mine

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to capture them

explanation.surface: A limpet mine, the kind a commando sticks to a ship, used by special forces ahead of a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: A limpet mine is a magnetic explosive, but the definition is the shellfish.

clue.text: Description of Kane, for example — captain's first in this oddly calm state

indicators.note: the first letter of captain
the odd-numbered letters of the two words

parts.note: Zen is a meditative calm

explanation.walkthrough: Citizen Kane is Orson Welles's 1941 film; its title word describes Kane.

clue.text: Off-colour setter taking bait occasionally — unlucky

indicators.note: every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: The setter, feeling poorly, takes the bait now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves; here 'setter' is Fed, who wrote this puzzle.

clue.text: Star announced support for record company's move overseas

parts.note: EMI is a British record label

parts.note: a star is a great, someone eminent

explanation.surface: A pop star declares the label's backing for a move abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: GREAT spoken sounds like GRATE, the metal frame that supports a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to live in another, which means relocating abroad.

clue.text: Quickly run through dance at a distance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
off means away, at a distance

explanation.surface: Dancing at a distance from one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to recite it rapidly and fluently.

clue.text: Enemy runs away from front …

indicators.note: the runs letter goes away from the word for front

parts.note: the fore is the front part
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An opponent flees from the front line, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an adversary or opponent.

clue.text: … runs away from case of deplorable valets possibly trashing vehicle

trashing means wrecking, so the vehicle is wiped out of the word

parts.note: valets are an example of servants
a van is a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis lets 'runs away from' serve again; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to abandon them, fleeing from them.

clue.text: Will blush given they're all naked — it's unreal

explanation.definitionFit: Illusive means based on illusion, deceptive and not real.

clue.text: Make a mess of hairpiece, occasionally sold for sport

clue.text: Mood tense over missing gold sovereign

explanation.definitionFit: One's temper is one's state of mind, as in a good or bad temper.

clue.text: Unnamed fell runner

explanation.definitionFit: A ski is one of the long runners on which a skier glides, as a sledge has runners.

explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring a claim against someone in court.

clue.text: Feature of theatre role — having boob exposed at the start

indicators.note: the start of the word exposed, its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: In a theatre the parterre is the pit, the seats behind the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The parterre is the ground-floor seating area in a theatre, one part of its layout.

clue.text: Reason for acting in new movie, capturing actor's essence
